investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 135–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and a full contract-gap failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval run.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots are currently occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is the most direct reading of 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector rules target a label that is only present on the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are simultaneously resource-exhausted. If the label set on those nodes changed, the effective schedulable pool could have shrunk further.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If concurrent remote-agent workloads (e.g., from other users or other eval runs) consumed all slots before this probe ran, the probe would see the same Unschedulable error transiently.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — peer-pod provider quota or cloud-side VM limit: the kata-containers peer-pod provider may have hit an external quota (e.g., cloud VM instance limit) that prevents new VMs from being allocated even if Kubernetes node capacity appears available.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing (Unschedulable)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-02 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes, preventing any new remote-agent pod from being scheduled. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner could not create an agent, and therefore produced no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is consistent across all three checks, indicating the VM-slot resource is fully consumed and preemption cannot free any slots. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure that blocked pod scheduling before the eval runner could reach the agent creation or state-polling steps, which is why the evidence object is empty (failed-check.evidence) and all required contract fields are missing (expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-detected infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a user-facing outage independently.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler failure pattern ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck 145s, latencyMs=148279.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, readyState, or state was ever captured because the pod never started.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent() could return (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905, line 1905: 'const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)').

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=153009, which is below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000 (source.infra/evals/status/features.json:184), so the check timed out on scheduling, not on a latency breach.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: the remote-agent-state contract requires readyState and state, neither of which can be populated without a running pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all three checks report the same scheduler message with zero preemption victims available, indicating the VM-slot quota is fully consumed and no existing pods are preemptible.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch has reduced the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules, leaving only 2 nodes to absorb VM-slot demand. If those 2 nodes are undersized or their VM-slot quota is too low for concurrent eval runs, transient exhaustion is likely.

Tertiary — concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs may be holding VM slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) failed in a previous run, orphaned pods could be occupying the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

Lower confidence — a cluster-level quota or resource limit change may have reduced the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes, but no configuration change evidence is present in the packet to support this.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workloads: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the stage of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the remote agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. Because the pod could not be scheduled within the eval timeout window (~135–148 s across all three checks), no agent was ever created, no runtime response was returned, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message containing "hello from aura") could not be satisfied. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 135–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and a full contract-gap failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval run.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots are currently occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is the most direct reading of 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector rules target a label that is only present on the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are simultaneously resource-exhausted. If the label set on those nodes changed, the effective schedulable pool could have shrunk further.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If concurrent remote-agent workloads (e.g., from other users or other eval runs) consumed all slots before this probe ran, the probe would see the same Unschedulable error transiently.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — peer-pod provider quota or cloud-side VM limit: the kata-containers peer-pod provider may have hit an external quota (e.g., cloud VM instance limit) that prevents new VMs from being allocated even if Kubernetes node capacity appears available.

This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure that blocked pod scheduling before the eval runner could reach the agent creation or state-polling steps, which is why the evidence object is empty (failed-check.evidence) and all required contract fields are missing (expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-detected infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a user-facing outage independently.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workloads: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the stage of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the remote agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. Because the pod could not be scheduled within the eval timeout window (~135–148 s across all three checks), no agent was ever created, no runtime response was returned, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message containing "hello from aura") could not be satisfied. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on both eligible nodes — concurrent workloads or a prior eval run may have consumed all available VM slots and they were not released before this run.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are at capacity, leaving zero schedulable nodes.
[Possible] A kata peer-pod VM from a previous eval run was not cleaned up (leaked), consuming a VM slot and reducing available capacity below the minimum needed for a new pod.
[Possible] The cluster was scaled down or a kata-capable node was cordoned/drained, reducing the pool of eligible nodes from its expected size.

[Lower confidence] A configuration change in the pod spec (node affinity, resource requests, or tolerations) introduced by a recent deployment could have tightened scheduling constraints, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the eval re-run succeeds immediately without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied VM slot that was released) rather than a persistent capacity shortage.

If kubectl or the cluster API shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and unoccupied on both eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but rather a misconfigured resource request or quota in the pod spec.
If the 4 non-kata nodes are shown to have been eligible (matching affinity/selector) at the time of the run, the node affinity mismatch diagnosis would need revision.

If a passing run of remote-agent-create is observed concurrently with this failure, the scheduling layer is not uniformly exhausted and the cause may be isolated to a specific pod configuration or namespace quota.

If the eval runner logs show that createAgent returned an error unrelated to Kubernetes scheduling (e.g., an API authentication failure or a missing configuration value), the Kubernetes scheduling diagnosis would be secondary to an earlier failure.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and reports available vs. allocated slots as evidence. This would surface exhaustion before a full scheduling timeout.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods remain in Pending or Running state after each eval cycle, catching resource leaks before they affect subsequent runs.

Add a remote-agents scheduling health check that specifically tests whether a minimal kata peer-pod can be scheduled (without running a full agent), with a shorter timeout, to detect node pool capacity issues independently of the full agent lifecycle.
Consider a sibling eval that checks the count of kata-capable nodes and their reported allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, alerting if the pool drops below a defined minimum threshold.
